title: Per-event game coverage report
description: One row of data/curated/event-games.jsonl for every selected event, saying whether the corpus carries rows for it. It keeps 'the source has no games for this event' from looking like 'nobody fetched this event': `recorded` means rows are present (games or series), `empty` means no rows are present while a recorded ScoreboardGames query named this event and the source returned none, and `missing` means no recorded query named it. `missing` is a claim about the recorded queries, not about the outside world: a payload whose query names the event in a shape this report cannot read would read as `missing`, so the query text is the evidence to check by hand. `games` and `matches` are counts of emitted rows, so a reader can reconcile them against the files.

state.description: `recorded`: at least one game is emitted for this event. `empty`: a recorded ScoreboardGames query named this event (its page or its source tournament) and returned no rows — measured on World Cyber Games 2013. `missing`: no recorded query addressed this event.

games.description: How many rows this event contributes to games.jsonl.

matches.description: How many rows this event contributes to matches.jsonl.
